brief: Increasing competition (MSFT's Maia chip becoming its primary inference chip, NVDA pursuing Reflection AI, China's CXMT advancing a memory product) is weighing on the AI trade by threatening the oligopoly narrative, extending a tech selloff (SOX below its 100-day average, KOSPI below its 200-day) even as tech positioning stays less stretched than this summer, so the note argues AI infra need not fall if broadening returns. US banks' Q3 reports starting today are framed as the catalyst that could extend broadening; a separate Q3 preview puts median YoY EPS growth at 8% for the SPX and 9% for the SXXP, with EU broadening still absent and EU positioning stretched versus the US. The desk is tactically bullish on global equities, long US and Asia (Japan, Korea, Taiwan) versus Europe, reasoning the US is overheating while Europe recovers from stagflation; EU broadening needs EGB spread stability first. France's budget debate starts today, with an Article 49.3 trigger risking a no-confidence vote; the EGB desk sees OATs as cheap but is not entering longs given the politics. In positioning, US hedge-fund exposure sits near its 46th percentile and roughly unchanged month-to-date, while EU exposure has fallen to around the 13th percentile.
